program.welcome: Beginners, families, and competitors are all welcome
about: {name} is the yo-yo and skill toy community for {area}. Yo-yos, kendama, spin tops, diabolo, juggling: if it takes practice and it's fun, it's welcome here. {welcome}.
Never touched a kendama? Grinding a contest routine? This is your crew. {loaners} Someone will always help you land your first trick.

pillars.title: Try Everything
pillars.text: Pick up a yo-yo, a kendama, or a spin top. Swap toys and find the one that clicks.

pillars.title: Learn
pillars.text: Experienced players love to teach. Ask for help with any trick.

pillars.title: Play
pillars.text: Jam sessions, trick battles, and games anyone can join.

pillars.title: Share
pillars.text: Swap tips, try other people's gear, and learn how to care for your toys.

program.meetup_blurb: A free, drop-in yo-yo and skill toy meetup. Beginners welcome, loaners available.
program.volunteer: We're run by volunteers. Help set up, greet first-timers, teach a trick, or plan an event. Every bit counts.
program.donate_text: Meetups are free, always. Donations cover string, loaner toys, and venue costs.
program.contact_note: First time? You don't need to email first. Just show up. But we're happy to answer questions.

loaners.yes: We bring loaner yo-yos and other skill toys to every meetup, so you don't need to bring anything.
loaners.no: Bring your toys if you have them. Don't have any? Email us and we'll try to have a spare.

cost.details: Meetups are free. No dues, no fees, no membership forms.

learn.title: Learn Skill Toys
learn.intro: Every skill toy starts the same way: one small trick, over and over, until it clicks. Pick a toy and start here.

basics.title: Yo-Yo
basics.text: Start with a responsive yo-yo. String to about 2 inches above your belly button, palm up, throw straight down.

basics.title: Kendama
basics.text: Hold the ken by the handle, let the tama hang still, and bend your knees as you pull it up.

basics.title: Spin Tops
basics.text: Wind the string tight from the tip up, then throw overhand and snap your wrist back.

basics.title: Diabolo & Juggling
basics.text: Diabolo: roll it along the string to start it spinning. Juggling: start with one ball, then two.

learn.levels_intro: One starter list for each toy. Land these and you're on your way.

levels.label: Kendama
levels.name: Kendama
levels.text: Knees bent, eyes on the tama.

learn.divisions_intro: Yo-yo contests group freestyles into styles. You don't need to compete, but it helps to know the names. Rules vary by contest, so check the event's rules page.

divisions.name: Single A
divisions.text: One yo-yo, string tricks. The most popular style.

divisions.name: Two-handed looping
divisions.text: Two responsive yo-yos looping around your hands at once.

divisions.name: Double A
divisions.text: Two yo-yos doing string tricks at the same time.

divisions.name: Offstring
divisions.text: The yo-yo isn't tied to the string. You launch it and catch it.

divisions.name: Freehand
divisions.text: A counterweight replaces the finger loop, so the whole setup flies.

learn.outro: Learning is faster in person. Bring your toys and questions to the next meetup.

faq.a: {name} is a yo-yo and skill toy club for {area}. We bring together players {ages}, from total beginners to contest players. {welcome}.
Not at all. Most people come to hang out, learn tricks, and have fun. Contests are one part of the hobby, not a requirement.
No. Kendama, spin tops, diabolo, juggling, poi and other flow arts, and any other skill toy are welcome. Bring what you love.

faq.q: When and where do you meet?
faq.a: {meetup}. We meet at {venue}, {address}. Come and go anytime during the meetup.
No. Just show up. If a meetup is ever cancelled, we post it on this site and our social media as early as we can.
Nothing. {loaners} Wear comfortable clothes you can move in.
Yes! All ages are welcome. Younger kids should come with a parent or guardian, especially the first time.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to do any tricks?
faq.a: No. Total beginners are just as welcome as experienced players. We'll help you with your first trick on any toy.
Try a few toys at a meetup first, then ask our members. They'll recommend a starter yo-yo or kendama for your budget.

faq.q: Is it cheating to learn on an unresponsive yo-yo?
faq.a: No. A landed trick is a landed trick. Classic tricks are worth learning on a responsive yo-yo too, but there's no wrong way to play.

faq.q: How do I become a member?
faq.a: Just come to a meetup. There's no sign-up. If you show up, you're part of the club.
Yes, please. Email {email} or talk to us at a meetup. We always need help setting up, greeting newcomers, and running activities.

faq.q: Can my organization partner with the club?
faq.a: Yes. We're open to venue partnerships, demos, workshops, and sponsorships. Email {email} with your idea.

safety.title: Keeping Meetups Safe
points: Kids are welcome. Younger kids need a parent or guardian with them. A parent or guardian is responsible for their own child at every meetup.
Club volunteers never take kids anywhere away from the group or the meetup space.
Give each player room. Check behind you before a big trick, and keep looping, offstring, diabolo tosses, and flow arts in open space.
Check your gear before you play. Worn yo-yo strings and frayed kendama strings can snap.
safety.photos: We sometimes take photos at meetups for this website and our social media. Tell a volunteer if you or your child would rather not be photographed. We never post a child's full name, and we take photos down whenever asked.

conduct.intro: {name} is built on the idea that yo-yos and skill toys should be fun and welcoming for everyone. That only works if people treat each other well. This code sets out what we expect from everyone in our community.
conduct.short: Be kind. Be welcoming. Don't make anyone feel unsafe or unwelcome. If you see something, say something.
applies: Everyone at our meetups and events, including players, parents, and spectators
Competitors and spectators at contests we run
Anyone in our online spaces and group chats
expected: Be respectful. Treat everyone with dignity, whatever their age, skill level, race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or background.
Be welcoming, especially to beginners and younger players. Everyone was new once.
Keep feedback encouraging. If someone asks for tips, help. Skip the harsh criticism.
Mind the space. Keep the venue clean, watch your yo-yo's reach, and look out for kids.
Respect decisions. Raise disagreements with organizers calmly and privately.
unacceptable: Harassment of any kind, including unwanted contact, following, or persistent unwanted attention
Photographing someone who asked not to be photographed
Discrimination, slurs, or jokes that put people down
Threats or intimidation, in person or online
Taking or damaging someone's gear without permission
Disruptive behavior that ruins the meetup for others
equipment: Ask before you borrow. Hand it back the way you got it.
Look before you throw. Big tricks, tosses, and flow arts need open space.
Replace worn strings, and stop if a toy is cracked or damaged.
Return loaner toys before you leave.
conduct.reporting: If something makes you uncomfortable, tell a club volunteer at the meetup or email us. We take every report seriously and keep it as private as we can.
conduct.consequences: Organizers may give a warning, ask someone to leave a meetup, or ban someone from future events, depending on what happened. For anything involving a child's safety, we will contact the venue and, where needed, the authorities.
